mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal income (PAYEMS) and real disposable income (RSAFS) month-over-month signals improved household balance sheets, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for four consecutive months, in the absence of offsetting wage growth, signals persistent labor market slack and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% per month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained high unemployment and weak payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained monthly CPI increases above 3% for six months.
